source.title: Stochastic Mirror Descent on Overparameterized Nonlinear Models
source.authors: Navid Azizan; Sahin Lale; B. Hassibi

record.file_problem: None; the supplied text includes the paper and supplementary material.
record.tranche_reason: Compares generalization after different stochastic mirror descent algorithms reach 100% training accuracy, testing how implicit regularization changes the train–test gap with a different optimizer family from the versions listed.
record.gate_note: The study reports test performance for MNIST and CIFAR-10 after fitting the training data. Its discussion of random-label capacity is background, not a result of this study.
record.test_reason: The study tests implicit regularization by stochastic mirror descent, but none of V1–V8. Natural-label interpolation alone does not test V1, and comparing fixed mirror potentials with SGD does not test V4's adaptive-optimizer comparison. Random-label capacity and adaptive-optimizer findings appear only as background citations.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors additionally establish conditional convergence and approximate proximity to the closest interpolating solution in the corresponding Bregman divergence, and experimentally find that each mirror's solution is closest among the sampled solutions under its corresponding divergence. Their generalization results motivate further study of regularizer choice.
record.recipe_differences: Uses stochastic mirror descent with `1`-, `2`-, `3`-, and `10`-norm potentials; the reported test comparison is not the adaptive-optimizer comparison in the listed original versions.
record.method_sensitivity: On CIFAR-10, test performance differs by mirror potential; `10`-norm is consistently best and `1`-norm consistently worst. On MNIST, all four methods achieve around 99% or higher accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: All four SMD methods reach 100% training accuracy and around 99% or higher MNIST test accuracy. On CIFAR-10 with ResNet-18 across eight initializations, l10-SMD consistently performs best and l1-SMD worst; the abstract explicitly ranks SGD between them.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Changing the mirror potential can change held-out performance despite perfect training accuracy, with differences depending on the dataset.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
record.problems: Test accuracies are not numerically transcribed in the supplied text for CIFAR-10; Figure 7 and Figure 13 show them, but the text only gives a qualitative ranking. The supplied text reports no uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: No random-label training or held-out random-label accuracy comparison with the same architecture and recipe.
No width sweep or test-error comparison beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison or test of local connectivity.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison, tuning-budget comparison, decoupled weight decay, or optimizer switching.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets or adapted training recipes.
No magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, correlation with generalization gaps, or ranking of generalization measures. Bregman distances to initialization measure a different construct.
No memorization-based example selection, removal, or retraining comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any listed version, but it supplies no eligible version-level verdict. States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8; this does not negate the reported accuracies or qualitative mirror ranking.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train on random labels or compare natural-label and random-label test accuracy.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected architectures.
Compares mirror descent potentials, not adaptive optimizers such as Adam against SGD or momentum SGD.
Does not vary batch size or compare batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets.
Does not measure sharpness or compare generalization measures.
Does not remove or retrain on selected training examples.
